faq: How many users can it handle afterwards?
We measure it. After the changes we run the test again and tell you the load where response times start to slip. We do not promise a number up front because it depends on your code and data.
Will scaling make my hosting bill much bigger?
Not necessarily. Caching often lowers cost. Auto scaling adds servers only when traffic rises and removes them after. We show the likely monthly range for each traffic level.
Do you test on my live site?
We prefer a staging copy, because heavy tests can slow real customers. If only live is possible, we run light tests at a quiet hour and agree the limit with you first.
Is my app ready to scale as it is?
Some apps need code changes first, for example if they store files on one server's disk. The test shows this, and we say clearly if the fix is bigger than the package.

desc:
Scaling your app for more traffic means finding where it slows down under load and fixing it before a launch or sale. Ecom Swift LLC runs load tests, adds caching or extra servers where they help and reports how much traffic the set-up can handle.

## What does scaling an app for more traffic mean?

Scaling means making your app keep working as the number of visitors grows. That can mean making each request cheaper, so one server serves more people, or adding more servers, so the work is shared. Often it means both.

Apps rarely fail evenly. One slow database query, one page without caching or one small server often becomes the bottleneck long before everything else does. Scaling work starts by finding that single weak point instead of buying bigger machines everywhere.

## Why testing before a busy day matters

A traffic spike is the worst time to learn your limits. A launch, a promotion, a press mention or a seasonal peak all bring visitors at once. If the app slows or crashes at that moment, you lose the attention you paid or waited for, and some visitors will not come back.

A load test replays realistic visits against a safe copy of your app and watches what happens. It shows which page slows first, which resource runs out and how the system behaves at double or triple the usual load. That is far cheaper than discovering the answer live.

## How scaling work improves reliability

Scaling work improves the experience for every visitor, not only during peaks. Caching makes common pages load faster. A better database plan or a read replica shortens queries. A load balancer lets one server fail without taking the site down. Automatic scaling adds capacity when traffic rises and removes it when it falls.

It also helps you plan money. Knowing how many visitors the current set-up handles, and what the next step would cost, lets you decide when to upgrade instead of reacting to an emergency. Results depend on your code, your data and the provider, so we report what the tests show and do not promise a fixed number.

## What a scaling engagement includes

- Load tests that mimic real visitor journeys, such as browsing, search, login and checkout.
- A bottleneck report that names the slowest parts of the system.
- Caching for pages, objects or database results where it is safe.
- Database tuning, a larger plan or a read replica for heavy read traffic.
- A load balancer in front of two or more app servers.
- Automatic scaling rules that add and remove servers as traffic changes.
- A CDN to serve images, scripts and other static files from nearby locations.
- A retest after changes, to confirm the improvement.
- Capacity notes in plain words for current and expected traffic levels.
- A spike plan for launches or sales, listing steps to take before and during the event.

## How we do the work

We begin by learning what you expect: the date of the event, the pages that matter and what a normal day looks like. We then write test scripts for those journeys and run them against a staging copy, or against production only if you ask and agree on a quiet window.

From the results we choose fixes in order of effect, apply them and test again so you can see the difference. Basic covers one key page and the first fixes. Standard adds caching, a load balancer and a second test across several flows. Premium adds automatic scaling, a read replica, a CDN, a spike plan and a handover call. Extra hosting costs, if any, are paid to your provider.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Test on a copy that matches production.
- Fix the slowest part first, then test again.
- Cache pages and files that rarely change.
- Plan extra capacity ahead of known events.
- Keep a way to return to the earlier set-up.

**Avoid:**
- Buying larger servers before finding the bottleneck.
- Load testing a live site without warning your team.
- Caching pages that show private user data.
- Assuming the set-up that worked last year still holds.
- Scaling the app while the database stays untouched.

## Who this is for

This service suits an online business planning a sale or product launch. It suits a startup whose app slows during peak hours and needs to know why. It also suits a team that expects a spike from a press feature or a campaign.

## What we need from you

Tell us the date of the event, the pages and actions that matter most and your expected visitor numbers. Share access to a staging copy if you have one. We never need your passwords. Access is given as a limited developer or team user in your own account.
